title: How moms can help their daughters build a healthy body image, with Janet Boseovski, PhD, and Ashleigh Gallagher, PhD

sentences.en: How often do you hear comments like this?
sentences.zh: 你多久听到一次这样的评论？

sentences.en: I'm going to be good and skip dessert tonight.
sentences.zh: 我今晚要乖一点，不吃甜点。

sentences.en: Or that actress looks amazing for her age.
sentences.zh: 或者，那个女演员保养得真好，看不出年龄。

sentences.en: Or that dress really flatters you.
sentences.zh: 或者，那条裙子真的很衬你。

sentences.en: Maybe you've even said a few of these things.
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至自己也说过这些话。

sentences.en: Senses like these might seem harmless or even positive, but they send messages to girls from a very young age about how to think about their own bodies and those of others.
sentences.zh: 这些话听起来似乎无害甚至是积极的，但它们从很小的时候就开始向女孩传递信息，教她们如何看待自己和别人的身体。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk to two psychologists about body image, child development, and how psychological science can help mothers guide their daughters
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与两位心理学家探讨身体形象、儿童发展，以及心理学科学如何帮助母亲引导女儿

sentences.en: toward a healthy relationship with their bodies.
sentences.zh: 树立健康的身体关系。

sentences.en: So what is body image and why is it important?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是身体形象？为什么它很重要？

sentences.en: How do kids understand body image from early childhood through the tween years?
sentences.zh: 从幼儿期到青少年早期，孩子们是如何理解身体形象的？

sentences.en: How does a parent's own body image affect their kids?
sentences.zh: 父母自身的身体形象如何影响孩子？

sentences.en: And how much sway do parents really have in this sphere, especially with social media, peers, and other influences all competing for kids' attention?
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体、同龄人和其他各种争夺孩子注意力的因素面前，父母在这个领域到底能有多大影响力？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，专门探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 我今天请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Janet Boziofsky, a developmental psychologist and professor of psychology at the University of North Carolina, Greensboro.
sentences.zh: 第一位是珍妮特·博齐奥夫斯基博士，她是一位发展心理学家，也是北卡罗来纳大学格林斯伯勒分校的心理学教授。

sentences.en: Her research has looked at children's understanding of the social world and the development of body image in children.
sentences.zh: 她的研究主要关注儿童对社会世界的理解以及儿童身体形象的发展。

sentences.en: She's published dozens of academic papers and is a member of the board of directors of the Jean Piaget Society and an editorial board member for the journals
sentences.zh: 她发表了数十篇学术论文，是让·皮亚杰学会的董事会成员，也是学术期刊

sentences.en: Social Development and the Journal of Experimental Child Psychology.
sentences.zh: 《社会发展》和《实验儿童心理学杂志》的编委会成员。

sentences.en: Next is Dr. Ashley Gallagher, who is a social psychologist and senior lecturer in psychology at UNC Greensboro.
sentences.zh: 接下来是阿什利·加拉格尔博士，她是北卡罗来纳大学格林斯伯勒分校的社会心理学家兼心理学高级讲师。

sentences.en: Her research interests include emotion, culture, group dynamics, and gender.
sentences.zh: 她的研究兴趣包括情感、文化、群体动力学和性别。

sentences.en: She has a longstanding interest in bridging the academic real-world gap and has worked in public policy research and as a research consultant.
sentences.zh: 她长期致力于弥合学术界与现实世界的鸿沟，曾从事公共政策研究并担任研究顾问。

sentences.en: Drs.
sentences.zh: 加拉格尔博士

sentences.en: Gallagher and Boziofsky are co-authors of a new book,
sentences.zh: 和博齐奥夫斯基博士是新书的合著者，

sentences.en: Beyond Body Positive, a mother's science-based guide for helping girls build a healthy body image, published in December by APA Books.
sentences.zh: 该书名为《超越身体悦纳：母亲帮助女孩建立健康身体形象的科学指南》，于12月由APA图书出版公司出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位做客我的节目。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Okay, so the title of the book is Beyond Body Positive.
sentences.zh: 好的，这本书的书名叫《超越身体悦纳》。

sentences.en: Why did you choose that title?
sentences.zh: 你们为什么选择这个书名？

sentences.en: What does it mean to go beyond body positive when thinking about a healthy body image?
sentences.zh: 在思考健康的身体形象时，“超越身体悦纳”意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, first we should say that there is the science on positive body image and then there is the social movement of body positivity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先我们要说明，一方面有关于积极身体形象的科学研究，另一方面有身体悦纳的社会运动。

sentences.en: And so we were pretty careful choosing this title, but we wanted to indicate that some of the means that we see in popular culture
sentences.zh: 所以在选择这个书名时我们非常谨慎，但我们想要指出的是，我们在流行文化中看到的一些方法

sentences.en: and some of the treatment of this topic in popular culture is perhaps oversimplified and that this is actually a really complex and deep topic.
sentences.zh: 以及流行文化对这个话题的一些处理方式，可能过于简单化了，而这其实是一个非常复杂且深奥的话题。

sentences.en: So we wanted to bring science to everyday moms and kind of tell them what it offers a little bit differently than just the cultural movement of body positivity.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们希望把科学带给普通妈妈，并告诉她们，科学所能提供的视角与单纯的身体悦纳文化运动有些许不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so the idea is that it's great if we can celebrate our bodies, but the way that we feel about our bodies is so much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们的观点是，如果我们能赞美自己的身体，那当然很好，但我们对身体的感受要复杂得多。

sentences.en: As your introduction, the great examples that you had illustrated, right?
sentences.zh: 正如你在介绍中那些精彩的例子所说明的那样，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's maybe it sounds like a great idea to just tell people to love their bodies, but most people have complicated relationships with their bodies.
sentences.zh: 所以，告诉人们去爱自己的身体听起来像是个好主意，但大多数人与自己身体的关系其实很复杂。

sentences.en: And we also think that a lot of the popular culture is so excessively focused on the body.
sentences.zh: 而且我们认为，许多流行文化过度关注身体了。

sentences.en: And so when we talk about protecting ourselves as women, hearing all the cultural messages that we hear, we really want to arm girls.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们谈到作为女性如何保护自己时，面对听到的所有文化信息，我们真的希望能武装女孩们。

sentences.en: It's almost like we're saying, you know, let's get ahead of the culture and go beyond body positivity because you are not just your body.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是在说，你知道的，让我们走在文化的前面，超越身体悦纳，因为你不只是你的身体。

sentences.en: You are so much more.
sentences.zh: 你远不止于此。

sentences.en: And how do we fit, you know, all of these other characteristics about you into this picture?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何将关于你的所有其他特质融入这幅图景中呢？

sentences.en: Because this one has been so overblown for girls and women.
sentences.zh: 因为这个特质在女孩和女性身上被过度渲染了。

sentences.en: Your book is directed specifically at moMs.
sentences.zh: 你们的书是专门针对妈妈们的。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, so moms are the primary attachment figure in most, there are different kinds of compositions of families.
sentences.zh: 是的，妈妈是大多数家庭中的主要依恋对象——当然家庭的构成有各种各样。

sentences.en: But in most families, mom is the primary attachment figure or whichever maternal guardian.
sentences.zh: 但在大多数家庭中，妈妈是主要的依恋对象，或者说是主要的女监护人。

sentences.en: She is the person that young girls look to.
sentences.zh: 她是年轻女孩仰望的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, our daughters are watching us.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们的女儿在注视着我们。

sentences.en: That might be a little overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点让人压力山大。

sentences.en: But if you think about the type of information they're getting from you, it's in your gestures.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想想她们从你这里得到的信息类型，就会发现它藏在你的举手投足之间。

sentences.en: It is in the things that you say about your body.
sentences.zh: 藏在你对自己的身体所说的话里。

sentences.en: So if you are feeling fat one day and you're saying that and your daughter is hearing that, that's influencing her.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你觉得某天自己胖了并把这话说了出来，而你的女儿听到了，这就会对她产生影响。

sentences.en: When mom eats differently from the rest of the family because she's dieting, that gets encoded even if, you know, nothing is said about that.
sentences.zh: 当妈妈因为节食而吃得和家里其他人不一样时，即使没有明说，这种信息也会被女儿接收到。

sentences.en: She's very influential.
sentences.zh: 她的影响力非常巨大。

sentences.en: And one reason that we can, you know, encourage starting early in terms of developing a healthy body image is that that is the time when she's most influential.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以可以鼓励从早期开始培养健康的身体形象，原因之一就是在这个阶段她的影响力最大。

sentences.en: That is the time when girls are observing her so much.
sentences.zh: 这是女孩们大量观察妈妈的时期。

sentences.en: And so she can get ahead of all the influencers and all the media and all those cultural sorts of influences that are going to come into play a little bit later.
sentences.zh: 因此，妈妈可以抢在所有网红、所有媒体以及稍后会发挥作用的各种文化影响之前，先入为主地发挥积极作用。

sentences.en: And I think oftentimes we think of body image as if it just developed independently in our own head
sentences.zh: 我想很多时候我们认为身体形象好像是在我们自己的脑海中独立发展的，

sentences.en: without this social interaction process going on.
sentences.zh: 而没有考虑到其中正在发生的这种社会互动过程。

sentences.en: And, you know, as a social psychologist, I see it as a fundamentally social process where there's exchange going on.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，作为一名社会心理学家，我认为这是一个根本上的社会过程，其中存在着双向交流。

sentences.en: And since mom is the early influencer for little girls, mom is participating in helping daughter build her body image even from a young age.
sentences.zh: 既然妈妈是小女孩早期的影响者，那么妈妈从很小的时候起就在参与帮助女儿构建身体形象。

sentences.en: So we were looking around at what else was out there when we first became interested in this topic.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们最初对这个话题感兴趣时，我们环顾四周，看看市面上还有什么。

sentences.en: And there just wasn't much out there at all that treated this as an interaction between the primary influencer mom and the young daughter.
sentences.zh: 结果发现几乎没有什么书把这当作主要影响者（妈妈）与年幼女儿之间的互动来处理。

sentences.en: So the, you know, the social nature of this process is hugely important and has been overlooked.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个过程的社会属性极其重要，但却一直被忽视。

sentences.en: Now, you offer advice for parents of girls ages three to 10.
sentences.zh: 现在，你们为3到10岁女孩的父母提供了建议。

sentences.en: How did you pick that particular age range?
sentences.zh: 你们是怎么选择这个特定年龄段的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So as a developmental psychologist, you know, looking at early social, emotional, cognitive development, we know that there's critical things happening in how the self is
sentences.zh: 作为一名发展心理学家，研究早期的社会、情感和认知发展，我们知道，在这个时期，自我概念的

sentences.en: constructed during this time.
sentences.zh: 构建正发生着关键的事情。

sentences.en: So children develop a sense of who they are, something called a categorical self when they are very young.
sentences.zh: 所以，孩子们在很小的时候就会发展出一种对“我是谁”的认知，这被称为分类自我。

sentences.en: It starts with basic things.
sentences.zh: 它从最基本的事情开始。

sentences.en: How old am I, right?
sentences.zh: 我几岁了，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm a girl and I'm three years old and already you are thinking about who you are, what activities you enjoy, what hobbies and skills you have.
sentences.zh: 我是个女孩，我三岁了。此时此刻，你已经在思考你是谁、你喜欢什么活动、你有什么爱好和技能。

sentences.en: And then we have these influences on, you know, what you are supposed to believe about your gender, what girls can do, what boys can do.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们会受到这些影响：关于你应该对自己的性别有什么信仰，女孩能做什么，男孩能做什么。

sentences.en: We have cognitive maturation happening over the course of this, these years that will affect how we have to convey information to you.
sentences.zh: 在这几年里，我们经历了认知成熟，这会影响我们向你传达信息的方式。

sentences.en: We have a growing understanding of what it means to eat, right?
sentences.zh: 我们对吃什么的理解越来越深刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Eating for nutrition, eating to be able to feel well, a growing understanding of what physical activity does for us.
sentences.zh: 为了营养而吃，为了感觉良好而吃，对身体活动能为我们带来什么有了越来越多的理解。

sentences.en: And so these are the key times to really sort of hammer in appropriate sort of ways of thinking about the self, apportioning all of these pieces of you into this self-concept.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是真正把适当的自我思考方式灌输进去的关键时期，把关于你的所有这些部分组合进这个自我概念中。

sentences.en: And we know that's growing over the course of early to late childhood in really key ways.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，从童年早期到晚期，这种认知在以非常关键的方式增长。

sentences.en: And then of course, we want to hit up the time when, you know, they're emerging preteen, tween years, and then you have peer and media influences coming in.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们希望赶在她们即将步入前青春期、十多岁这一时期之前介入，因为那时同龄人和媒体的影响就会接踵而至。

sentences.en: And again, you know, that's going to be another critical time where you're going to emphasize things like
sentences.zh: 同样，你知道，这将是另一个关键时期，你需要强调诸如

sentences.en: critical thinking around the media and understanding what you see on Instagram or whatever other social platform isn't always real.
sentences.zh: 围绕媒体的批判性思维，并理解你在Instagram或任何其他社交平台上看到的东西并不总是真实的。

sentences.en: It doesn't represent typical people.
sentences.zh: 它并不代表普通人。

sentences.en: You know, these are not your role models, probably for the most part.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些在很大程度上可能并不是你的榜样。

sentences.en: And so you've just got key social, emotional, cognitive development happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，关键的社会、情感和认知发展正在发生。

sentences.en: You have emergence of complex emotions as they get older, so they start to feel shame.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄的增长，她们开始涌现出复杂的情感，比如她们开始感到羞耻。

sentences.en: And certainly for girls, all of the body messages that they hear, you know, we need to work through those emotions and work through sort of the messages that they're
sentences.zh: 当然，对于女孩来说，她们听到的所有关于身体的信息，你知道，我们需要陪她们疏导这些情绪，并在这些信息

sentences.en: hearing with them as they're happening.
sentences.zh: 发生的同时陪她们一起解读。

sentences.en: The popular thing has been to hand girls a book when they're preteens.
sentences.zh: 过去常见的做法是在女孩进入前青春期时塞给她们一本书。

sentences.en: And already so much of the self has developed and so many of those messages have already been taken in.
sentences.zh: 但那时大部分自我意识已经形成，许多那样的信息已经被全盘接受了。

sentences.en: And we're saying, actually, we can preempt that.
sentences.zh: 而我们的观点是，其实我们可以先发制人。

sentences.en: We can build a stronger self and say, I'm going to hear these messages, but I can actually actively choose to reject these messages.
sentences.zh: 我们可以建立一个更强大的自我，并说：我会听到这些声音，但我实际上可以主动选择拒绝这些声音。

sentences.en: I can construct a self that is stronger than what I'm hearing out there.
sentences.zh: 我可以构建一个比外界听到的声音更强大的自我。

sentences.en: Dr. Gallagher, let me ask you, what should moms and maybe even dads be saying to their daughters early on to help them develop a positive body image?
sentences.zh: 加拉格尔博士，我想问您，妈妈们甚至爸爸们应该在早期对女儿说些什么，来帮助她们建立积极的身体形象？

sentences.en: Well, one thing is to talk about the body in ways that appreciate its function.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一点就是以欣赏其功能的方式来谈论身体。

sentences.en: And that's when you're talking about the body, but certainly talk about the girl in terms of the other qualities that make her who she is and who you love.
sentences.zh: 当然可以谈论身体，但一定要从构成她是谁、以及你所深爱的那些其他品质来谈论这个女孩。

sentences.en: So many times with my own daughter, you know, when people would meet her when she was a young girl for the first time, they would say, oh, you're so pretty.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，以我自己的女儿为例，你知道的，当人们第一次见到她还是个小女孩的时候，他们会说：“哦，你长得真漂亮。”

sentences.en: And, you know, that's a wonderful compliment, certainly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这当然是一个美好的赞美。

sentences.en: And they were well-intentioned, but they were immediately drawing out the focus or putting the focus on her physical appearance and, you know, getting to know
sentences.zh: 他们是出于好意，但他们立刻把焦点引向了或者说把焦点放在了她的外表上，而没有去了解

sentences.en: her and who she is and how smart she is and the clever things she does.
sentences.zh: 她是谁、她有多聪明以及她所做的那些聪明的举动。

sentences.en: All of that is so much more important than talking about appearance.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都比谈论外表要重要得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, kids are watching us much earlier than we think they are.
sentences.zh: 所以，孩子们观察我们的时间比我们想象的要早得多。

sentences.en: And so, being careful about how we talk about other people and making sure that we aren't talking about them in terms of their appearance or their bodies, because, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们要小心我们谈论其他人的方式，确保我们不是在用他们的外表或身体来评判他们，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: hopefully we all understand that there's so much more than that, as Janet was saying a little bit ago.
sentences.zh: 希望我们都明白，正如珍妮特刚才所说，人远不止于此。

sentences.en: And also making sure that, you know, when we see things on television together that we're watching
sentences.zh: 同时还要确保，当我们一起看电视

sentences.en: or out in public, that we help girls, you know, interpret that and understand it appropriately.
sentences.zh: 或在公共场合看到某些事物时，我们要帮助女孩去解读并恰当地理解它们。

sentences.en: And, you know, again, just making sure that we are taking the focus off of appearance and putting on other aspects of who people are that are so much more important.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，还是要确保我们将焦点从外表上移开，放在比外表重要得多的其他人格特质上。

sentences.en: We also want moms to not be doing things like talking negatively about themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们还希望妈妈们不要做一些诸如消极谈论自己的事情。

sentences.en: Like, I can't believe, you know, how much weight
sentences.zh: 比如，“我简直不敢相信，

sentences.en: I've gained or I look terrible in these jeans.
sentences.zh: 我胖了多少斤”或者“我穿这条牛仔裤难看死了”。

sentences.en: I can't go out on the beach because I don't like the way I look in my swimsuit.
sentences.zh: “我不能去海滩，因为我讨厌自己穿泳衣的样子。”

sentences.en: All of those, you know, with a little girl who's watching you, she, you know, is directing her thoughts to, well, I hadn't been thinking previously about how I look in a
sentences.zh: 所有这些话，如果被一个正在看着你的小女孩听到，她就会把思绪转向：嗯，我以前没有想过自己穿泳衣好不好看，

sentences.en: swimsuit, but now do I look bad in my swimsuit too?
sentences.zh: 但现在我是不是穿泳衣也很难看？

sentences.en: So, just, you know, managing the types of things that we say about other people and ourselves and making sure they're not negative, but also making
sentences.zh: 所以，只需管理好我们对别人和自己所说的话，确保它们不是消极的，同时也要

sentences.en: sure that they're not overly focused on appearance and the body.
sentences.zh: 确保它们不会过度关注外表和身体。

sentences.en: But what do you say to your daughter when that stranger or friend or other family member says, oh, you're so pretty?
sentences.zh: 但是，当陌生人、朋友或其他家庭成员对女儿说“哦，你真漂亮”时，你对女儿说些什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's, you know, that's an interesting one because we don't want to offend family members.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个有趣的问题，因为我们不想冒犯家庭成员。

sentences.en: And we talk about that in the book, like strategies for when, you know, grandma or grandpa comes
sentences.zh: 我们在书里讨论过这一点，比如当爷爷奶奶

sentences.en: over and they talk about, she's such a pretty little girl and we encourage family, you know,
sentences.zh: 过来并说“她是个多漂亮的漂亮小女孩”时的应对策略，我们鼓励家庭成员，

sentences.en: we encourage moms to have direct contact with family members and conversations about, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们鼓励妈妈们与家人直接沟通并进行对话，比如：

sentences.en: I'm really trying to help Amy's math skills and it would be wonderful if you compliment her on these things that she's working on, right?
sentences.zh: “我真的很努力在帮艾米提高数学能力，如果你能夸奖她正在努力做的事情，那就太好了”，对吧？

sentences.en: And same with your daughter.
sentences.zh: 对女儿也是如此。

sentences.en: So, when someone says that to her, it's partly her understanding that that, while it is a compliment and she can, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，当有人对她这样说时，一方面是要让她明白，虽然这是一个赞美，她当然

sentences.en: certainly take it graciously, that that doesn't mean that she has to consider it as very important, right?
sentences.zh: 可以大方地接受，但这并不意味着她必须把这看作是最重要的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: That she can, A, you know, just let it go, but she can also point out other things that she's working on and redirect the conversation and learn to do that.
sentences.zh: 她可以A，让它过去，但她也可以指出她正在努力的其他事情，并转移话题，学会这样做。

sentences.en: We encourage women to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们鼓励女性这样做。

sentences.en: Women engage in fat talk, right?
sentences.zh: 女性经常参与“身材闲聊”，对吧？

sentences.en: I feel so fat.
sentences.zh: “我觉得自己好胖。”

sentences.en: Oh, you're not fat.
sentences.zh: “噢，你不胖。”

sentences.en: Who's fat?
sentences.zh: “谁胖了？”

sentences.en: Who's gained weight?
sentences.zh: “谁长胖了？”

sentences.en: This is something that culturally we've almost been taught to do and that's applauded, right?
sentences.zh: 这是文化上几乎教会我们去做且被社会赞许的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, again, it's about consciously steering the conversation away from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这同样关乎有意识地将对话从这些话题上引开。

sentences.en: And we see body image as something that women can direct themselves, but I don't think our generation learned that.
sentences.zh: 我们将身体形象视为女性可以自己主导的事情，但我不认为我们这一代人学过这个。

sentences.en: You know, we just sort of received the messages and now we're saying, actually,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们只是接收了这些信息，而现在我们在说，实际上，

sentences.en: we have the power to say, no, we reject this and we want to teach girls that they have the power to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们有力量说“不，我们拒绝这些”，并且我们想教导女孩们，她们也有力量做到这一点。

sentences.en: You've alluded to the fact that the moms, women adults, struggle with their own body image.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到妈妈们和成年女性自身也在与身体形象作斗争。

sentences.en: And in the book, you use a phrase, normative discontent, that sums it up.
sentences.zh: 在书中，你们用了一个词“规范性不满”来总结这一现象。

sentences.en: Being unhappy with your body is basically seen as normal for women.
sentences.zh: 对自己的身体感到不满意，在女性中基本上被视为一种常态。

sentences.en: How can mothers help their daughters build a healthy body image when it's probably something that they themselves are struggling with?
sentences.zh: 当母亲们自己可能也在苦苦挣扎时，她们该如何帮助女儿建立健康的身体形象？

sentences.en: That's a great question because we do acknowledge in the book that mom's body image development is ongoing as well.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，因为我们在书中确实承认，妈妈自身的身体形象发展也在进行中。

sentences.en: This is not something that ends when she becomes an adult.
sentences.zh: 这并不是在成年后就结束的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, her body's going to go through changes continuously as well, like pre-partum and postpartum and menopause, for example.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，她的身体也会不断经历变化，比如孕前、产后和更年期等。

sentences.en: And so, moms are at different points when they are doing the parenting and having these interchanges with their daughters.
sentences.zh: 因此，妈妈们在育儿和与女儿进行这些互动时，正处于不同的阶段。

sentences.en: So, certain things might be, you know, coming to one mom's mind that is not troubling another mom's mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，某些事情可能会浮现在某个妈妈的脑海中，而另一个妈妈则不会为此苦恼。

sentences.en: But one of the things that we think is beneficial here is that if we kind of treat this as a habit and work on it as ways of
sentences.zh: 但我们认为有益的一点是，如果我们把这当作一种习惯，并将其作为我们谈论身体或

sentences.en: talking about our body or orienting toward our body and making sure that those are respectful,
sentences.zh: 看待身体的方式来加以改进，并确保这些方式是尊重的，

sentences.en: you know, that that becomes habitual and it becomes a way of thinking that can benefit moms wherever they are, you know, in their current adult development of body image as well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这会变成一种习惯，变成一种思维方式，无论妈妈们身在何处，甚至在她们目前成年后的体象发展中，都能让她们受益。

sentences.en: So, we think that this has benefits not only for the daughter and teaching her and actively and intentionally modeling for her
sentences.zh: 所以，我们认为这不仅对女儿有益，能教导她、积极且有意地为她树立榜样，

sentences.en: how she should, you know, treat her body, that moms will in turn come to treat their bodies in this way as well.
sentences.zh: 展示她应该如何（你知道的）对待自己的身体，妈妈们反过来也会以这种方式对待自己的身体。

sentences.en: So, it's never too late to learn.
sentences.zh: 所以，学习永远不会嫌晚。

sentences.en: We think not.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得不会。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: Hopefully.
sentences.zh: 希望如此。

sentences.en: For all of us.
sentences.zh: 为了我们所有人的。

sentences.en: Let's dig into some of the science of child development, which is important to the crux of your whole book.
sentences.zh: 让我们深入探讨一些儿童发展的科学，这对你整本书的核心观点非常重要。

sentences.en: And you talk about three age ranges.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了三个年龄段。

sentences.en: You've got three to four, five to seven, and eight to ten.
sentences.zh: 你有三到四岁、五到七岁以及八到十岁。

sentences.en: So, how can we, can we break this down and then talk first about the youngest?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何，能把这些拆解开，然后先谈谈最小的年龄段吗？

sentences.en: What is important to know developmentally about three and four-year-olds when you're thinking about starting to build a healthy body image?
sentences.zh: 当你想开始建立健康的体象时，关于三岁和四岁儿童的发展，有哪些是重要的知识？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, first, you know, we'll be realistic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，你知道的，我们要现实一点。

sentences.en: They're three and four, so they can't hold a lot of information in mind.
sentences.zh: 他们才三四岁，所以记不住太多信息。

sentences.en: So, not to put too much pressure on moms who are thinking, I mean, come on, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，不要给那些心想“拜托，真的吗？”的妈妈们施加太多压力，

sentences.en: Look at, look at this, right?
sentences.zh: 看看，看看这个，对吧？

sentences.en: They're very intelligent, but they cannot process, of course, information the way that adults do.
sentences.zh: 他们非常聪明，但当然，他们无法像成年人那样处理信息。

sentences.en: The key thing
sentences.zh: 关键的一点是

sentences.en: I'll say first that cross-cuts all of these ages is, and the literature supports this at any age, is not focusing on the weight of the child and the body shape of the child.
sentences.zh: 我首先要说的是，贯穿所有这些年龄段的是——文献在任何年龄段都支持这一点——不要把重点放在孩子的体重和体形上。

sentences.en: You know, there can be an inclination if you feel like your child is heading toward being overweight or you're concerned to say things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你觉得你的孩子有超重的趋势或者你有所担忧，你可能会倾向于说某些话。

sentences.en: Those things are unhelpful.
sentences.zh: 那些话是没有帮助的。

sentences.en: The literature has established that very well, so we discourage that.
sentences.zh: 文献已经非常充分地证实了这一点，所以我们不鼓励这样做。

sentences.en: When children are three and four, you know, girls are three and four, we want to
sentences.zh: 当孩子们三四岁的时候，你知道，女孩子们三四岁的时候，我们希望

sentences.en: already be looking at things like gender stereotypes and debunking those.
sentences.zh: 已经开始关注性别刻板印象之类的事情并打破它们。

sentences.en: So, girls are told stuff like, you know, she's so delicate.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们会对女孩说这样的话，你知道，她好娇气啊。

sentences.en: You know, the frilly dresses, all of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些荷叶边连衣裙，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And we want to, there's nothing wrong with showing those sides, of course, of girlhood, but we want to encourage the other sides, right?
sentences.zh: 我们想要，当然，展示女孩这一面并没有错，但我们想要鼓励其他方面，对吧？

sentences.en: Being adventurous.
sentences.zh: 要有冒险精神。

sentences.en: We want to encourage descriptions about strong.
sentences.zh: 我们希望鼓励对“坚强”的描述。

sentences.en: We want to also take the focus off of appearance-based descriptions, right?
sentences.zh: 我们还希望将焦点从基于外表的描述上移开，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, look at how well you jump.
sentences.zh: 比如，看你跳得多好。

sentences.en: I'm so impressed at how hard you worked on that drawing, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我对你画画那么努力印象深刻，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: Because this age group really divides the world in terms of good things and bad things.
sentences.zh: 因为这个年龄段的孩子看待世界，基本上是根据好事和坏事来划分的。

sentences.en: The other thing we want to try to do is not promote good and bad with food.
sentences.zh: 我们要努力做的另一件事，是不要在食物上助长好与坏的观念。

sentences.en: That food is good or bad for you.
sentences.zh: 即某种食物对你来说是好是坏。

sentences.en: You know, food is food.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，食物就是食物。

sentences.en: It's energy.
sentences.zh: 它是能量。

sentences.en: Certainly, some foods have more nutritional value.
sentences.zh: 当然，有些食物营养价值更高。

sentences.en: We all know this, but we don't want to start instilling shame and morality around food because that's where down the line you start to get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道这一点，但我们不想开始围绕食物灌输羞耻感和道德感，因为随着时间的推移，你就会在那里遇到麻烦。

sentences.en: Again, going back to your introduction, like, I was good today because of what I ate or didn't eat, right?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，回到你的引言，就像，我今天表现很好，因为我吃了什么或没吃什么，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, those kinds of messages are important, not having food morals.
sentences.zh: 所以，这类信息很重要，不要有食物道德观。

sentences.en: And then we also talk about body respect, which is learning early the habits of taking care of your body.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还讨论身体尊重，也就是尽早学会照顾身体的习惯。

sentences.en: And at three and four, it's enjoying movement.
sentences.zh: 在三四岁的时候，这就是享受运动。

sentences.en: Movement is fun.
sentences.zh: 运动是快乐的。

sentences.en: It's not supposed to be punitive.
sentences.zh: 它不应该是惩罚性的。

sentences.en: It should be something that we enjoy.
sentences.zh: 它应该是我们享受的事情。

sentences.en: So, in this youngest group, those are the kinds of things that we emphasize doing.
sentences.zh: 所以在最小的这个群体中，这些就是我们强调要做的事情。

sentences.en: We have actual suggestions for activities and things that moms can do with their daughters, books that they can read together, but really just getting away from gender
sentences.zh: 我们有针对活动的实际建议以及妈妈们可以和女儿一起做的事情，她们可以一起阅读的书籍，但实际上只是为了摆脱性别

sentences.en: stereotypes and also, you know, broadening and exploring the concept of the self beyond appearance.
sentences.zh: 刻板印象，同时（你知道的）拓宽和探索超越外表的自我概念。

sentences.en: But if you're a mom of a girl about that age, and she starts getting into the whole Disney princess thing, should you be worried?
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个有着这个年龄左右女孩的妈妈，而她开始迷上整个迪士尼公主系列，你应该担心吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And we delved into that literature a little bit in the book.
sentences.zh: 我们在书里稍微探讨了一下相关文献。

sentences.en: And it's no one thing that's going to cause a problem.
sentences.zh: 单凭某一件事情是不会导致问题的。

sentences.en: We do know girls have a preference for the certain type of doll, right?
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道女孩对某种特定类型的玩具有偏好，对吧？

sentences.en: The stereotypical, beautiful, white, thin doll.
sentences.zh: 那种刻板的、漂亮的、白人、瘦削的娃娃。

sentences.en: And we ideally want to provide a wider variety of toys.
sentences.zh: 而我们理想的做法是提供更多样化的玩具。

sentences.en: We want to have a variety of exposure to movies that they're watching.
sentences.zh: 我们希望让他们接触各种各样他们正在观看的电影。

sentences.en: And they are actually broader these days.
sentences.zh: 而且如今它们实际上更广泛了。

sentences.en: So, the research is kind of mixed on the effects.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于这些影响的研究可以说是毁誉参半。

sentences.en: And I think it's mixed because in parenting, if you see a diversity of things, if you present your child with a diversity of things, then that's going to help.
sentences.zh: 我认为之所以毁誉参半，是因为在育儿过程中，如果你看到多样化的事物，如果你向孩子展示多样化的事物，那就会有所帮助。

sentences.en: If you are careful about conversations around these kinds of characters and you dialogue with your daughter about these things, that's also helpful.
sentences.zh: 如果你对围绕这些类型角色的对话保持谨慎，并与你的女儿就这些事情进行对话，这也是有帮助的。

sentences.en: So, you know, we don't really take an approach of ruling anything out completely.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们并没有采取完全排除任何事物的态度。

sentences.en: It's really the total package that matters the most because, I mean, they do love their Disney princesses.
sentences.zh: 真正最重要的是整体套餐，因为，我的意思是，她们确实很喜欢她们的迪士尼公主。

sentences.en: And, you know, that'll be an important part of relating to their peers is knowledge about
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，了解迪士尼公主将是与同龄人建立关系的一个重要部分，

sentences.en: those Disney princesses because their friends will be talking about those things.
sentences.zh: 因为她们的朋友会谈论这些事情。

sentences.en: So, we don't want to raise little children that are going to be excluded from their peer groups because that's very important for them too.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们不想抚养那些会被同龄群体排挤的小孩，因为这对他们来说也非常重要。

sentences.en: So, I think it's just more about responsible consumption of those types of media.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为这更多的是关于对这些类型媒体的负责任消费。

sentences.en: So, when we get to the age group five to seven, what changes?
sentences.zh: 那么，当我们进入五到七岁这个年龄段时，有什么变化？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, now, you know, they're exposed a little bit more to the outside world.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在，你知道的，他们更多地接触到了外面的世界。

sentences.en: They've started school.
sentences.zh: 他们开始上学了。

sentences.en: The schedule is a little more structured.
sentences.zh: 日程安排更有条理了一些。

sentences.en: They're being exposed to more people.
sentences.zh: 他们接触到了更多的人。

sentences.en: And so, here we talk about learning about gender roles outside of the home, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，在这里我们讨论的是了解家门之外的性别角色，对吧？

sentences.en: You know your home composition, but you're going to see the kinds of jobs that people do, the kinds of discussions that your peers have.
sentences.zh: 你知道你的家庭构成，但你会看到人们从事的工作，看到同龄人进行的讨论。

sentences.en: And so, you're still continuing to sort of facilitate and monitor ideas about gender.
sentences.zh: 所以，你仍在继续某种程度上促进和监督关于性别的观念。

sentences.en: You want to encourage activities that, you know, are suitable for all genders that are not necessarily sex-typed.
sentences.zh: 你想要鼓励那些（你知道的）适合所有性别、不一定非要贴上性别标签的活动。

sentences.en: Girls at this age become more sensitive to inside personality characteristics.
sentences.zh: 这个年龄的女孩对内在的个性特征变得更加敏感。

sentences.en: So, not just behaviors, but inner characteristics.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅仅是行为，还有内在特征。

sentences.en: So, starting to facilitate those, like, look at how creative you are, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，开始促进这些方面，比如，看你多有创意啊，对吧？

sentences.en: Or, you're such a kind person, right?
sentences.zh: 或者，你是一个如此善良的人，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, you're building that self-concept irrespective, again, of what she looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以，你正在建立这样的自我概念，同样与她的外表无关。

sentences.en: For some kids, you start to see sort of the bullying that can come with looking a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 对于某些孩子，你会开始看到那种由于外表稍有不同而带来的霸凌现象。

sentences.en: We always talk about, as developmental psychologists, that there can't be any place for bullying.
sentences.zh: 作为发展心理学家，我们总是说，绝对不能给霸凌留出任何空间。

sentences.en: That is when, if you're seeing that sort of thing, parents need to be reporting that to school authorities.
sentences.zh: 那正是家长需要向学校当局举报的时候，如果你看到了那种事情的话。

sentences.en: So, there has to be a zero-tolerance policy for things like that.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于诸如此类的事情，必须采取零容忍政策。

sentences.en: It's a great idea to get girls involved in a sport.
sentences.zh: 让女孩参与一项运动是个好主意。

sentences.en: It's kind of fun to watch kids of this age try to play a sport, but that encourages, you know, leadership, being part of a team.
sentences.zh: 看这个年龄的孩子尝试进行一项运动挺有趣的，但这能鼓励（你知道的）领导力、团队合作精神。

sentences.en: And again, by doing that activity, you're just enjoying the activity, and you're not thinking about what you look like.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，通过进行这项活动，你只是在享受活动，而没有去想你长什么样。

sentences.en: You're just out there in it, right?
sentences.zh: 你只是置身其中，尽情享受，对吧？

sentences.en: And how freeing is that?
sentences.zh: 那是多么令人解脱啊！

sentences.en: You're paying attention a little bit more to the type of media that you expose her to.
sentences.zh: 你对你让她接触的媒体类型给予了更多的关注。

sentences.en: So, you know, parents have different views on what children can watch, but of course, you should be watching.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，家长对孩子能看什么有不同的看法，但当然，你应该关注。

sentences.en: And here, you also start to see a little bit of the emergence of emotions like shame, the self-conscious emotions.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你还会开始看到一些诸如羞耻感之类的情绪萌芽，即自我意识情绪。

sentences.en: It's mostly reserved for the next group, but again, depending on your child.
sentences.zh: 这主要留给下一个群体，但同样，这取决于你的孩子。

sentences.en: So, some kids are very sensitive, some kids less so.
sentences.zh: 所以，有些孩子非常敏感，有些则不然。

sentences.en: You usually know what kid you have, what girl you have.
sentences.zh: 你通常知道你有什么样的孩子，你有什么样的女孩。

sentences.en: And that's where, too, if there are comments about her body that make her feel shame, it's important to address those and say that comments that other people make about you
sentences.zh: 正因如此，如果有关于她身体的评论让她感到羞耻，解决这些问题就很重要，并指出其他人对你的评论

sentences.en: are their problem.
sentences.zh: 是他们的问题。

sentences.en: They're inappropriate, and they really have nothing to do with you.
sentences.zh: 它们是不恰当的，而且真的跟你没有任何关系。

sentences.en: And so, those kinds of feelings are understandable, but that does not reflect your personhood, and that should not be part of the fabric of who you are.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种感觉是可以理解的，但这并不反映你的人格，也不应该成为构成你本质的一部分。

sentences.en: And then when we get to the ages 8 to 10, what changes?
sentences.zh: 然后，当我们进入八到十岁时，有什么变化？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: So, this one is quite different because now you're dealing with much more influence of peers.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一个非常不同，因为现在你要应对来自同龄人的更多影响。

sentences.en: It's not that mom is no longer influential, but the peers are now taking more control over the social context.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说妈妈不再有影响力，而是同龄人现在对社交环境有了更多的控制。

sentences.en: There's more exposure to media.
sentences.zh: 接触媒体的机会更多了。

sentences.en: So, again, watching what they're consuming and starting to have critical conversations about what they're seeing and how it represents women and is this okay or not okay?
sentences.zh: 所以，同样的，关注他们在消费什么，并开始对他们所看到的内容以及它是如何代表女性的进行批判性对话，这可以接受吗？还是不可以？

sentences.en: Is this real?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is this not real?
sentences.zh: 这不是真的吗？

sentences.en: It's a pre-puberty time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个青春期前期。

sentences.en: Girls develop at very different rates.
sentences.zh: 女孩发育的速度非常不同。

sentences.en: We want to prepare them for the change that's going to happen in their body because that's where a lot of these self-conscious emotions like shame really come into play.
sentences.zh: 我们希望为她们身体即将发生的变化做好准备，因为正是从这里开始，许多诸如羞耻感之类的自我意识情绪真正发挥了作用。

sentences.en: And we want to preempt that by saying body changes are perfectly normal.
sentences.zh: 我们希望通过这样的话来先发制人：身体的变化是完全正常的。

sentences.en: They're going to happen throughout your entire life.
sentences.zh: 它们会贯穿你的整个人生发生。

sentences.en: This is the beginning of it.
sentences.zh: 这只是个开始。

sentences.en: It might feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人感觉不舒服。

sentences.en: It probably will feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 它很可能会让人感觉不舒服。

sentences.en: And that's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系的。

sentences.en: And everybody's feeling that way, even though it doesn't seem that way, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都有这种感觉，尽管看起来不像，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the early developing girls are upset that they're developing early.
sentences.zh: 因为发育较早的女孩对她们过早发育感到心烦意乱。

sentences.en: The late developing girls are jealous that the early developers are getting attention.
sentences.zh: 发育较晚的女孩则嫉妒那些发育较早的人受到了关注。

sentences.en: And nobody's happy with where they are.
sentences.zh: 没有人对自己的现状感到满意。

sentences.en: We also see at this age, a decline in their, their self-concept positivity.
sentences.zh: 我们在这个年龄还会看到，她们的自我概念积极性有所下降。

sentences.en: So that's been documented in the literature where they were once more optimistic about themselves and about other people.
sentences.zh: 这已经在文献中得到了记录，她们曾经对自我以及对其他人都更加乐观。

sentences.en: There's a bit of a decline because now it's kind of, you're seeing the harsh reality of the world a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 会有所下降，因为现在某种程度上，你更多地看到了世界的残酷现实。

sentences.en: And you're also learning in school that maybe you're not the best at everything.
sentences.zh: 而且你在学校里也了解到，也许你不是每件事都做得最好。

sentences.en: Maybe someone is better at math or better at this and you start engaging in social comparison.
sentences.zh: 也许有人数学更好，或者这个更好，然后你开始进行社会比较。

sentences.en: So now we have a whole host of other things, right?
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有一大堆其他事情，对吧？

sentences.en: To sort of handle and talking about, you know, how to work on your skills and not compare yourself to other people, right?
sentences.zh: 需要某种程度上处理，并且讨论（你知道的）如何提升你的技能，而不是把自己和别人作比较，对吧？

sentences.en: So talking about the physical, but also talking about these emotions they might be having around feeling inadequate in general is going to be really important.
sentences.zh: 所以，谈论生理方面固然重要，但谈论她们可能因普遍感到不够优秀而产生的这些情绪，也将非常重要。

sentences.en: And in this age group, you can definitely start emphasizing holistic health more because they know a lot more about biological processes.
sentences.zh: 在这个年龄段，你绝对可以开始更多地强调整体健康，因为她们对生物过程了解得更多了。

sentences.en: They understand food a lot better.
sentences.zh: 她们对食物的理解好多了。

sentences.en: So you want to really emphasize like you live in your body and you may not love your body every day and that's totally fine, but you will, oh, you should always care and
sentences.zh: 所以你真的想要强调，比如你生活在自己的身体里，你可能不会每天都喜欢自己的身体，这完全没问题，但是你将，哦，你应该始终关爱并

sentences.en: respect for your body, have respect for your body, right?
sentences.zh: 尊重你的身体，对身体保持尊重，对吧？

sentences.en: And have the behaviors that are associated with that.
sentences.zh: 并采取与之相关的行为。

sentences.en: And again, that's bringing in the health behavior without that physical appearance piece.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这是在引入健康行为，而没有外表那一部分。

sentences.en: We don't, we don't need to have that in order to have the, the, uh, the health behavior benefit.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要，我们不需要为了获得，那个，嗯，健康行为的好处而拥有外表那部分。

sentences.en: And we think that's an important thing to educate girls.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是对女孩进行教育的重要内容。

sentences.en: A lot of people have called for more education for children around health literacy.
sentences.zh: 很多人呼吁对儿童进行更多关于健康素养的教育。

sentences.en: Now you stopped at age 10.
sentences.zh: 现在你停在了10岁。

sentences.en: Doesn't girls' attention to their bodies really take off when they hit puberty?
sentences.zh: 女孩对身体的关注在她们进入青春期时不是真的会猛增吗？

sentences.en: So I'm not going to accuse you of taking the easy route, but, but is that your next book?
sentences.zh: 所以我不会指责你走了捷径，但是，但是，那是你的下一本书吗？

sentences.en: So one of the reasons that we didn't focus on that is there are books that focus on that particular period.
sentences.zh: 我们没有关注那个原因之一，是有一些书籍专门关注那个特定时期。

sentences.en: And our perspective is that's great, but a lot of the, the damage, so to speak, or a lot of the influence has already happened.
sentences.zh: 我们的观点是，那很好，但是许多，所谓损害，或者说许多影响已经发生了。

sentences.en: So in our view, it must start earlier, especially in the culture that we're living in now, where, you know, we were pummeled with this information.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们看来，它必须从更早开始，尤其是在我们现在生活的文化中，你知道的，我们被这些信息狂轰滥炸。

sentences.en: We didn't even have social media and now it's just coming at you from every single direction as a girl.
sentences.zh: 我们当时甚至还没有社交媒体，而现在作为一个女孩，这些信息正从各个方向朝你扑面而来。

sentences.en: And so this is why we felt we needed to fill that niche and we needed specifically to deal with that early mother and daughter relationship.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们觉得我们需要填补这个空白，我们需要专门处理那种早期的母女关系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Mom will still be important, of course, in the adolescent years, but, you know, relative to peers in the media, her influence has now taken a little bit of a backstage presence.
sentences.zh: 当然，妈妈在青春期依然扮演着重要角色，但你知道，相对于媒体中的同龄人，妈妈的影响力现在退居了一点二线。

sentences.en: And so when we were looking at what else was out there, there is a lot of things, you know, good resources out there about media consumption,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们审视其他领域时，有很多很好的资源，你知道的，关于媒体消费的资源，

sentences.en: social media consumption, and the influence of peers.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体消费，以及同龄人的影响力。

sentences.en: So we just really saw this spot that was unaccounted for, which was the early years when mom has the most influence over the daughter
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的看到了这样一个未被填补的空白，那就是母亲对女儿影响最大的早期阶段，

sentences.en: and hopefully can inoculate her from some of the stuff that will hit in puberty and beyond.
sentences.zh: 并且希望能够帮她抵御一些即将在青春期及以后涌现的问题。

sentences.en: That makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 这非常在理。

sentences.en: Now let's talk about food and eating, because there are so many messages in our culture that emphasize thinness for girls and women.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来谈谈食物和饮食，因为我们的文化中充斥着强调女孩和女性纤瘦的各种信息。

sentences.en: So how can moms of very young children help them navigate those messages and feel good about themselves?
sentences.zh: 那么，极年幼孩子的母亲如何帮助她们应对这些信息并建立自我认同感呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, that's a tough one because not only do you have those messages, you also have a lot of just picky eating in some kids and particularities, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很难办，因为不仅有这些信息，有些孩子还特别挑食和讲究，对吧？

sentences.en: And in certain children.
sentences.zh: 而且在某些孩子身上尤为明显。

sentences.en: I think a lot of it is modeled in the home.
sentences.zh: 我认为很大程度上这需要在家庭中以身作则。

sentences.en: We know from research that providing options for kids is really important.
sentences.zh: 我们从研究中得知，为孩子提供多种选择非常重要。

sentences.en: And that means providing options for all foods and not ruling out certain foods.
sentences.zh: 这意味着为所有食物提供选择，而不排除某些特定食物。

sentences.en: At the same time, learning to impose restrictions of where you're sort of using, you know, induction that you do with kids where it's,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，学会施加限制，也就是运用你对孩子使用的那种引导方式，

sentences.en: you're kind of asking a question and setting a rule at the same time.
sentences.zh: 也就是你一边提问，一边设定规则。

sentences.en: Is it a good idea to eat this cupcake right now?
sentences.zh: 现在吃这个纸杯蛋糕是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That type of thing where it's not that the cupcake is good or bad, but there are times for cupcakes and times that, you know, maybe you shouldn't be having that cupcake because
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的情况，并不是说纸杯蛋糕是好是坏，而是说吃纸杯蛋糕有特定的时候，而有些时候，你知道的，你或许不应该吃那个纸杯蛋糕，因为

sentences.en: it's almost time for bed or you've already had two cupcakes and how are you going to feel?
sentences.zh: 快到睡觉时间了，或者你已经吃了两个纸杯蛋糕了，你会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: You know, you can model appropriate behavior by having family mealtimes where possible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，尽可能通过安排家庭进餐时间来树立合适的行为榜样。

sentences.en: That's certainly not possible for all family compositions, but that's been shown to be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 这当然不适用于所有家庭结构，但事实证明这非常有用。

sentences.en: Not overemphasizing that something is healthy, even though it's tempting to do that, that often backfires.
sentences.zh: 不要过分强调某样东西很健康，尽管这样做很诱人，但往往会适得其反。

sentences.en: It's good for you.
sentences.zh: 这对你有好处。

sentences.en: Eat it, right?
sentences.zh: 吃掉它，对吧？

sentences.en: That's compelling.
sentences.zh: 这很有说服力。

sentences.en: So really just presenting different options, having children get involved in meal preparation as they get older so that they have some choices, but also allowing for preferences.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上就是提供不同的选择，让孩子们在大一点的时候参与备餐，这样他们就有了一些选择权，同时也允许他们有偏好。

sentences.en: Some children don't like certain foods and they don't have to like every single vegetable.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子不喜欢某些食物，他们不必喜欢每一种蔬菜。

sentences.en: They don't have to like every single thing.
sentences.zh: 他们不必喜欢每一样东西。

sentences.en: So also just letting them be their own person and not being overly rigid, but trying to offer a wide variety
sentences.zh: 所以，也要让他们做自己，不要过于死板，而是尝试提供丰富多样的食物，

sentences.en: of foods and trying to discuss how you feel and why during a sports activity, you might eat this type of food.
sentences.zh: 并尝试讨论你的感受以及为什么在运动时你可能会吃这种食物。

sentences.en: But at a birthday party, of course, you're going to have cake and you should have cake if you want the cake, right?
sentences.zh: 但在生日派对上，你当然会吃蛋糕，如果你想吃蛋糕，你就应该吃，对吧？

sentences.en: Things like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So differentiating between everyday eating versus special occasion eating, and that can be done without emphasizing diet culture at all.
sentences.zh: 因此，要区分日常饮食和特殊场合饮食，这完全可以在不强调节食文化的情况下做到。

sentences.en: So those are kind of the key pieces there.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是其中的关键部分。

sentences.en: And movement comes down to things like modeling, again, behavior as a family, going for walks, participating in activities you enjoy, and not presenting it as
sentences.zh: 至于运动，同样归结为作为家庭树立行为榜样、去散步、参与你喜欢的活动，而不是将其呈现为

sentences.en: something that is punishing, which I think for so many girls and women, athletics became
sentences.zh: 一种惩罚性的东西，我认为对于太多的女孩和女性来说，体育运动变得

sentences.en: unappealing because it was associated with you're doing this to, you know, account for the chocolate bar you ate.
sentences.zh: 没有吸引力，是因为它与“你做这个是为了弥补你吃的巧克力棒”联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Which is, again, not the message we want.
sentences.zh: 而这，再次强调，并不是我们想要传达的信息。

sentences.en: We want you to find movement that, you know, makes you feel good in your body and that is good for your body.
sentences.zh: 我们希望你找到能让你在身体上感觉良好且对身体有益的运动方式。

sentences.en: And you can model a wide variety of behaviors.
sentences.zh: 你可以树立各种各样的行为榜样。

sentences.en: You can hike and walk as a family.
sentences.zh: 你们可以全家一起远足和散步。

sentences.en: We talk about a lot of cheap and free things you can do.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了很多你可以做的廉价且免费的事情。

sentences.en: There's
sentences.zh: 比如

sentences.en: YouTube fun dance videos.
sentences.zh: YouTube 上的趣味舞蹈视频。

sentences.en: It's really about instilling the value again for them of, I enjoy this thing, plus it's also good for me.
sentences.zh: 这真的在于向她们灌输这样一种价值观：我喜欢这件事，而且它对我有益。

sentences.en: But the modeling behavior for those things, and especially for eating too, is going to be critical.
sentences.zh: 但为这些事情树立榜样，尤其是对饮食而言，将是至关重要的。

sentences.en: And some of it too is they're influenced by what their peers eat.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分原因也是她们会受到同龄人饮食习惯的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you're just going to have to sort of work through that.
sentences.zh: 而你只需要顺其自然地去应对。

sentences.en: You know, if everybody has this snack in their lunchbox, suddenly your child is interested in that snack.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果每个人的饭盒里都有这种零食，你的孩子突然也会对这种零食感兴趣。

sentences.en: And, you know, we can give in to some of those things shortly.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们可以短暂地迁就一下其中一些事情。

sentences.en: Well, what about dads and other males who might be in the household, especially brothers?
sentences.zh: 那么，家里的爸爸和其他男性，尤其是兄弟，情况又如何呢？

sentences.en: I know I grew up with two brothers and, you know, one way that they could really get me was to call me fat.
sentences.zh: 我知道我是和两个兄弟一起长大的，你知道，他们能真正拿捏我的方法之一就是叫我胖子。

sentences.en: You know, that was a big tease.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是一个很大的取笑点。

sentences.en: How can they help with body positivity and what can moms do, what can the readers of your book do to work with the men in their lives?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能为身体积极性提供帮助，妈妈们能做什么，你书中的读者能做什么来与他们生活中的男性合作？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, you know, moms need to let dad in on the focus that we're now going to have, which is not on appearance and not on body shape.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，你知道，妈妈们需要让爸爸了解我们现在要关注的重点，也就是不关注外表和体型。

sentences.en: So getting dad on board with not talking about, you know, other people's bodies and how they look.
sentences.zh: 所以让爸爸也赞同不讨论，你知道的，其他人的身体以及他们的外表。

sentences.en: That's going to be important.
sentences.zh: 这将是很重要的。

sentences.en: And dad's also talking with their daughters about things other than how pretty they are.
sentences.zh: 而且爸爸也要和女儿们谈论除了她们有多漂亮之外的事情。

sentences.en: So some of the same advice that we've been giving to moms here is just as applicable for fathers.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们这里给妈妈们的一些建议同样适用于爸爸们。

sentences.en: Now, brothers are a tougher case.
sentences.zh: 现在，兄弟们是个更棘手的情况。

sentences.en: And Janet may want to comment on the brothers.
sentences.zh: 詹妮特可能想对兄弟们发表一些看法。

sentences.en: But for many of the same things that we're talking about for moms to change, we want dads to do that as well.
sentences.zh: 但对于我们讨论的妈妈需要改变的许多事情，我们也希望爸爸们能做到。

sentences.en: So when dad's watching football or other sports, you know, maybe not drawing attention to the way that people's bodies look or in talking about the functions instead.
sentences.zh: 所以当爸爸在看足球或其他体育比赛时，你知道，或许不要把注意力吸引到人们的体型上，而是去谈论功能。

sentences.en: Wow, how strong that person is.
sentences.zh: 哇，那个人多强壮啊。

sentences.en: Or look at that flip they did.
sentences.zh: 或者看他们做的那个翻转动作。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊艳了。

sentences.en: Instead of, you know, commenting on appearance.
sentences.zh: 而不是，你知道的，对外观评头论足。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's tricky because there's less research on men and certainly on siblings as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很棘手，因为针对男性以及兄弟姐妹的研究确实较少。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we did try to dig up what there is.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们确实努力挖掘了现有的研究。

sentences.en: Fathers are influential.
sentences.zh: 父亲很有影响力。

sentences.en: If fathers focus on obsession with appearance, then actually there is an influence on daughters.
sentences.zh: 如果父亲专注于对外表的痴迷，那么实际上会对女儿产生影响。

sentences.en: If they comment on their daughter's weight, again, weight comments are a no-no.
sentences.zh: 如果他们评论女儿的体重，同样地，体重评论是绝对不行的。

sentences.en: So having an agreement within the family.
sentences.zh: 所以在家庭内部达成一致。

sentences.en: And that means getting siblings on board and actively saying, in this house, we don't comment on people's weight.
sentences.zh: 这意味着让兄弟姐妹也加入进来，并明确表示：“在这个家里，我们不评论别人的体重。”

sentences.en: Like that could be a conversation for the doctor, you know, the pediatrician, if that's a necessity medically.
sentences.zh: 这可以成为与医生谈论的话题，你知道的，如果是医学上的必要情况，可以和儿科医生谈。

sentences.en: But otherwise, we don't focus on that in this house.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，在这个家里我们不关注这个。

sentences.en: And so if a sibling is doing that, that sibling needs to be taught to be respectful.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有兄弟姐妹这样做，就需要教导这个兄弟姐妹学会尊重。

sentences.en: We do think that, you know, there could be ideally a book written for boys about how to navigate the culture of girls and women too, right?
sentences.zh: 我们确实认为，你知道的，理想情况下可以为男孩写一本书，关于如何应对女孩和女性的文化，对吧？

sentences.en: And for boys too, to be fair, I mean, there are demands on their own body image.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，对男孩来说也是如此，我的意思是，他们自己的身体形象也面临着要求。

sentences.en: We couldn't cover that.
sentences.zh: 我们没能涵盖这一点。

sentences.en: Again, not a lot of literature.
sentences.zh: 同样，相关文献并不多。

sentences.en: I have a doctoral student examining ideas about muscularity and male, you know, masculinity and ideas that boys get from things like Marvel Comics.
sentences.zh: 我有一位博士生正在研究关于肌肉发达、男性气概的想法，以及男孩们从惊奇漫画（Marvel Comics）等事物中获得的观念。

sentences.en: So they have their own pressures that are happening.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也有自己正在承受的压力。

sentences.en: They're not as strong.
sentences.zh: 它们没有那么强烈。

sentences.en: Certainly, they're not as pervasive as what we see for women.
sentences.zh: 当然，它们不像我们在女性身上看到的那样普遍。

sentences.en: But teaching boys to be sensitive through their own experience of that, right?
sentences.zh: 但是要通过男孩自身的经历来教导他们保持敏感，对吧？

sentences.en: If you're the skinny gangly kid who's being made fun of as a boy, well, you know all too well the pain of that.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个被嘲笑骨瘦如柴的男孩，好吧，你对那种痛苦再清楚不过了。

sentences.en: But showing the respect for other people and again, putting the emphasis on who we are as people and having just sort of house rules and
sentences.zh: 但要表现出对其他人的尊重，再次强调，要把重点放在我们作为什么样的人上面，制定一些诸如家规之类的东西，

sentences.en: explaining that when you leave the house, not everyone has those rules.
sentences.zh: 并解释说当你离开家时，并不是每个人都有这些规则。

sentences.en: But those are things you can take with you.
sentences.zh: 但这些是你可以随身携带的东西。

sentences.en: Other people can do what they wish.
sentences.zh: 其他人可以随心所欲。

sentences.en: You're not here to lecture to other people to talk about weight or not to talk about weight, but you can decide these are our values and this is what we do and this is our thing.
sentences.zh: 你在这里不是为了向其他人说教该谈论体重还是不谈论体重，但你可以决定这些是我们的价值观，这就是我们所做的，这就是我们的风格。

sentences.en: And again, that's like a protective barrier, right?
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这就像一道保护屏障，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't have to let it become part of you.
sentences.zh: 你不需要让它成为你的一部分。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about cultural differences.
sentences.zh: 我们花一分钟来谈谈文化差异。

sentences.en: Do you offer advice from moms and daughters from different racial or ethnic backgrounds or does the same advice apply no matter what background you have?
sentences.zh: 你们是否为来自不同种族或族裔背景的妈妈和女儿提供建议，还是说无论你有什么背景，同样的建议都适用？

sentences.en: I think the same general advice applies, which is celebrating and
sentences.zh: 我认为一般的通用建议是适用的，那就是赞美和庆祝

sentences.en: other aspects of your self-concept than your appearance.
sentences.zh: 你自我概念中除了外表之外的其他方面。

sentences.en: But certainly looking into the literature, we found that there are different specific appearance concerns between various cultural or racial groups.
sentences.zh: 但通过查阅文献，我们确实发现不同的文化或种族群体之间存在着不同的特定外表担忧。

sentences.en: So the specific concerns are going to be different that need to be addressed.
sentences.zh: 因此，需要解决的具体担忧将是不同的。

sentences.en: Is this an issue around weight that the girl is talking about or that the mom is talking about?
sentences.zh: 这是女孩或妈妈正在谈论的关于体重的问题吗？

sentences.en: Is this an issue about hair or about, you know, skin condition?
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于头发或，你知道的，皮肤状况的问题吗？

sentences.en: Or there's just a variety of kind of special topics that differ by group.
sentences.zh: 或者只是一系列因群体而异的各种特殊话题。

sentences.en: But the fundamentals there are the same, which is that sort of taking the investment out of our appearance and putting that in other aspects of ourself is beneficial for everybody.
sentences.zh: 但其中的基础是一样的，那就是把我们对外表的投入转移到自我的其他方面，这对每个人都有益。

sentences.en: What should you do about other close figures in your kids' lives?
sentences.zh: 对于孩子生活中的其他亲密人物，你应该怎么做？

sentences.en: Say you've got a grandparent or a family friend who is sending unhelpful messages.
sentences.zh: 比方说，你有一个祖父母或家庭朋友正在发出无益的信息。

sentences.en: You know, do you talk to the individual who's doing it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是去跟那个这么做的人谈谈吗？

sentences.en: Do you talk just to your daughter?
sentences.zh: 你是只和女儿谈谈吗？

sentences.en: Do you let it slide?
sentences.zh: 你是顺其自然置之不理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how should people navigate those situations?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们应该如何应对这些情况？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, ideally, again, depending on the age of the child and then depending on the nature of the relationship with the person, you know, is this a person that
sentences.zh: 你知道，理想情况下，同样取决于孩子的年龄，然后取决于与该当事人的关系性质，你知道，这是一个

sentences.en: you see frequently?
sentences.zh: 你经常见到的人吗？

sentences.en: Is this a person that the child is exposed to all the time?
sentences.zh: 这是一个孩子一直接触的人吗？

sentences.en: If it's an all the time sort of thing and the relationship is close, then we would encourage parents to say, yeah, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果这是一种持续存在的情况并且关系密切，那么我们会鼓励父母说，是的，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm really working on this sort of thing with her and this is why.
sentences.zh: 我真的在和她一起努力改进这方面的事情，原因就在这里。

sentences.en: And could you, you know, the way to do it is to say, could you help?
sentences.zh: 你能，你知道的，方法就是说，你能帮帮忙吗？

sentences.en: Not to say you're doing something wrong, but to just say, we're really trying to emphasize this, these kinds of skills in Kim, for example.
sentences.zh: 不是说你做错了什么，而是说，我们真的在努力强调这一点，比如在金（Kim）身上培养这些技能。

sentences.en: And, you know, it would be so helpful for you to talk about those things with her and try to reinforce the positive versus pointing
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你能和她谈谈这些事情，并努力强化积极的一面，而不是指出

sentences.en: out the negative, which is, you know, what we do in parenting.
sentences.zh: 消极的一面（你知道，这是我们在育儿中常做的），那将会有多大帮助啊。

sentences.en: So it's almost like you're trying to enforce or use that strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎就像你在试图强制执行或使用这种策略。

sentences.en: But I think being direct about it is fine.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对此表现得直接一点是没问题的。

sentences.en: And then from the daughter's end explaining that, again, some people will bring these things to you because we are in a world where people focus a lot on how people look.
sentences.zh: 然后从女儿的角度解释说，同样，有些人会把这些事情带到你面前，因为我们身处一个人们非常关注外表的社会。

sentences.en: So you're going to hear things and people will say things.
sentences.zh: 所以你会听到一些话，人们也会说一些话。

sentences.en: And again, it's up to you.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这取决于你自己。

sentences.en: How do you want to take that information, right?
sentences.zh: 你想要如何接受这些信息，对吧？

sentences.en: If you see your appearance as a small part of yourself, then this should not hurt you.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为外表只是你很小的一部分，那么这不应该伤害到你。

sentences.en: And that's our goal here is we're building someone who is broader than that, who if they receive a comment
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的目标，我们正在培养一个胸怀更广阔的人，如果她们收到这样的评论，

sentences.en: like that, it's that's not going to carry their day, because they are a strong person with interests and skills and talents.
sentences.zh: 那不会毁了她们的一天，因为她们是一个有兴趣、有技能、有才华的坚强的人。

sentences.en: And so here's this person that comes along and says something pretty superficial about you.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有这样一个人走过来，对你说了些相当肤浅的话。

sentences.en: Maybe it's upsetting.
sentences.zh: 也许这令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Maybe it's actually not.
sentences.zh: 也许其实并没有。

sentences.en: Maybe it's flattering.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一种奉承。

sentences.en: Either way, the message is the same that you can kind of let it roll off, right?
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，传达的信息都是一样的，你可以随风而去，对吧？

sentences.en: And it doesn't change who you are or how your value as a person.
sentences.zh: 它不会改变你是谁，也不会改变你作为人的价值。

sentences.en: But yes, I think, you know, we need to sort of explain it to girls, too, because I think the first time any girl gets that type of comment,
sentences.zh: 但是是的，我认为，你知道，我们也需要向女孩们解释这一点，因为我认为任何女孩第一次听到那种类型的评论时，

sentences.en: especially if it's embarrassing, it's jarring.
sentences.zh: 尤其是如果感到尴尬的话，那是令人震惊的。

sentences.en: Someone singles you out often publicly.
sentences.zh: 有人把挑出来，通常还是公开的。

sentences.en: Oh, she has her father's legs or something like that, right?
sentences.zh: 哦，她随了他爸爸的腿或者诸如此类的话，对吧？

sentences.en: And people do that and they think it's harmless.
sentences.zh: 人们会这样做，并且认为这无伤大雅。

sentences.en: But you don't know how that's being interpreted.
sentences.zh: 但你不知道这会被如何解读。

sentences.en: You don't know if there's a fraught relationship there.
sentences.zh: 你不知道其中是否存在紧张的关系。

sentences.en: There are so many reasons why it's just not a great idea to say those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 有太多原因表明，说这种话绝对不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: And you might even have it in your head as a compliment, but it isn't taken that way or it's misunderstood.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能在脑海里把它当成一种赞美，但对方并不这么认为，或者被误解了。

sentences.en: And so things like that, you want to explain that sometimes people will say these things and we don't have to hate those people or be mad at them.
sentences.zh: 所以像这样的事情，你要解释说有时候人们会说这些话，我们不必讨厌那些人或对他们生气。

sentences.en: We can just, again, choose how we interpret that information.
sentences.zh: 我们只需再次选择我们如何解读这些信息。

sentences.en: Because as Ashley was saying before, you know, we exist in the social sphere.
sentences.zh: 因为正如阿什利（Ashley）刚才所说，你知道，我们存在于社会圈子中。

sentences.en: We need to get along with people.
sentences.zh: 我们需要与人和睦相处。

sentences.en: So we're not going to walk around lecturing everybody about body image.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会到处去对每个人的身材形象评头论足。

sentences.en: It's more that for us internally, we've learned how to protect ourselves and how to handle those little things that come our way.
sentences.zh: 更确切地说，对我们自己而言，我们学会了如何保护自己，如何应对那些迎面而来的小事情。

sentences.en: I think a big key here is teaching the girl to be intentional about what she lets in and what she keeps out.
sentences.zh: 我认为这其中的一个关键，就是教导女孩要有意识地去选择接纳什么、排斥什么。

sentences.en: Oftentimes we act as if body image just happens to us or, you know, our views about, you know, our body or our appearance just kind of happen to us.
sentences.zh: 通常我们表现得好像身材形象是自然而然发生在我们身上的，或者说，你知道的，我们对身体或外表的看法好像就是那么凭空产生的。

sentences.en: But we can take an active role in that.
sentences.zh: 但我们完全可以在其中发挥积极主动的作用。

sentences.en: And that's a huge emphasis in our book is not treating this as a passive process, but rather seeing yourself as the manager of your own self-concept and your body image.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们书中的一个重点，即不要把这当作一个被动过程，而是要让自己成为自身自我概念和身材形象的管理者。

sentences.en: And so teaching her from the early age that, you know, you don't just have to take this and you don't just have to accept, you know, what others say or what they do.
sentences.zh: 因此，从小就教导她，你知道的，你不必逆来顺受，也不必全盘接受别人所说或所做的一切。

sentences.en: You're in charge of thinking about how your body, the way that you want to do it.
sentences.zh: 你可以按照自己想要的方式去主导对身体的思考。

sentences.en: And just to wrap up, you know, you had to read a lot of literature in order to write this book.
sentences.zh: 最后总结一下，你知道的，为了写这本书，你们阅读了大量的文献资料。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, as you were digging through, did you come up with sort of dead ends or the areas where you feel like we really need a lot more research?
sentences.zh: 我在想，当你们深入钻研时，有没有遇到死胡同，或者觉得亟需更多研究的领域？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at just the compositions of different kinds of families, we don't know much about that, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果只看不同类型家庭的构成，我们对此其实知之甚少，对吧？

sentences.en: It's usually the nuclear traditional family, a lot more about different cultures and cultural pressures, you know, integrating into the regular world.
sentences.zh: 以往通常都是核心传统家庭，关于不同文化、文化压力以及如何融入主流世界的研究则要多得多。

sentences.en: And then if you're part of any kind of subculture or ethnic minority, right, how do you handle those issues?
sentences.zh: 再比如，如果你属于某种亚文化群体或少数族裔，对吧，你该如何处理这些问题？

sentences.en: Issues around boys and men, issues around fathers and daughters, a lot of fathers are just not comfortable.
sentences.zh: 围绕男孩和男人的问题，围绕父亲和女儿的问题，许多父亲其实感到很不自在。

sentences.en: And then it is left to mom.
sentences.zh: 然后这些就全落在了妈妈身上。

sentences.en: In our focus group, a lot of moms talked about things like that, where it's kind of on them.
sentences.zh: 在我们的焦点小组中，许多妈妈都谈到了类似的情况，感觉重担全压在她们身上。

sentences.en: And that's a lot of pressure.
sentences.zh: 这带来了巨大的压力。

sentences.en: But men also feel like, oh, wait, like, is this my topic?
sentences.zh: 但男人们也会觉得，等等，这归我管吗？

sentences.en: Is this is a little uncomfortable to talk about my daughter and her body with her?
sentences.zh: 跟女儿讨论她和她的身体，是不是有点难以启齿？

sentences.en: So what do I do?
sentences.zh: 那该怎么办？

sentences.en: And then it can get all awkward, understandably.
sentences.zh: 可想而知，事情可能会变得很尴尬。

sentences.en: So I think in all of those arenas, we need good scientific research.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在所有这些领域，我们都需要优秀的科学研究。

sentences.en: I mean, you can find tons of advice on social media from all of the influencers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以在社交媒体上从各种网红那里找到大量的建议。

sentences.en: But the bottom line is, you know, we need the science, we need systematic work on all this stuff, so we can actually steer people in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 但最根本的是，我们需要科学，需要对所有这些内容进行系统化的研究，这样才能真正引导人们走上正确的方向。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天做客。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这次访谈真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I'm sure our listeners are going to learn a lot from hearing you and potentially reading your book.
sentences.zh: 我相信我们的听众听了你们的分享，并且去读了你们的书之后，一定会受益匪浅。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们来。

sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 speakingofpsychology.org 上，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 以及其他收听播客的平台上找到《心理学聊天》往期的节目。

sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢我们的节目，请关注我们并留下评价。

sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的节目有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。
